transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I've just been having some trouble at work lately. During our long sales strategy meetings, I... I just keep getting up. I know I'm supposed to stay seated, but I end up finding excuses to get out of my chair... like just to refill my water, or pace by the printer for a minute. So... yeah, that's mostly what made me come in.
Has this tendency to move around during meetings been a lifelong pattern for you, or is this a relatively new development?

Um... I guess it's not really new. It goes back way before high school. 

My... elementary school teachers used to write notes about it, I think. They'd say I was bright, but... that I rushed through things too much. And that I talked out of turn. I guess I also forgot my homework a lot back then... and my desk was always just stuffed with half-finished papers. 

So... yeah. It's been a long time.
Do you often find yourself acting or speaking without thinking about the consequences, even when you know you probably shouldn't?
Um... I don't think so. I mean, I don't really do that. I usually know what I'm doing, so... no, I haven't really noticed that.
Do you often find that you have trouble maintaining your focus on tasks or activities for a long period of time, such as when you are working on a project or reading?

Yeah... I guess so. Um... like in those strategy meetings I mentioned, or... if I'm reading a client brief. I'll start out fine, but after a few minutes, I just realize I've been staring at the same slide or paragraph. And I won't really have any idea what the last point was. So... yeah, I guess that happens.
Beyond getting up during meetings, do you often feel an internal sense of restlessness or find it difficult to sit still even when you are trying to relax at home?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I feel restless at home. I mean, when I'm trying to relax, I just... relax, I guess. I haven't really noticed feeling like I can't sit still then.
Do you frequently lose things that are necessary for your work or daily tasks, such as your keys, wallet, or important documents?

Um... yeah, I suppose I do. I just... I feel like I'm always hunting for things I need for work. Like my headset, or... client one-pagers. My keys. Or even just... the notebook I was using like ten minutes earlier. So... yeah, that happens.
In your work, do you often make careless mistakes or fail to pay close attention to details?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I make a lot of careless mistakes. I mean, I try to be careful with my work. I haven't really noticed that being an issue.

Looking at the last six months, would you say you have struggled with these difficulties—like losing things or losing focus—consistently across all areas of your life, including both your work and your home life?
Um... I guess so? I mean, I don't really know if it's everywhere. I just... I mostly notice it when it causes a problem, I guess. I'm not really tracking it.

Looking back at the last six months, would you say that you have consistently experienced the need to move around or fidget in settings other than your work meetings, such as when you are at home or socializing?

Um... no, not really. I don't think I do that. I mean, I might shift around a bit if I'm uncomfortable, but... no, I wouldn't say I have to move around constantly. I just... I don't really think about it.
Over the past six months, how many times per week, on average, would you say you have felt the urge to fidget with your hands or feet, or felt like you were 'driven by a motor'?

I don't know... I don't really keep track of that. I don't think I feel like a motor is driving me. Maybe I fidget sometimes, but... I don't know how many times a week. It's not something I pay attention to.
